speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with acute diarrhea; to help me identify the cause, could you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, along with the severity of your watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, this is highly suggestive of an antibiotic-associated colitis. We need to confirm this immediately.
